steps: Uncrate
Remove the wood crating top and supports, the plastic cover and the brick pack from the firebox. Fit the firebricks only once the stove is in its final location and the chimney is installed.
Floor protector
Continuous non-combustible ember protection on a combustible floor: USA 16" (406 mm) front and 8" (203 mm) to the sides of the door opening; Canada 18" (457 mm) firing side, 8" (203 mm) other sides.
Position to clearances

Place stove and protector to the single- or double-wall clearance chart; alcove max. depth 3', min. height 7'. Reduce clearances only with shielding approved under CSA B365 / NFPA 211 and by local authorities.
Confirm the chimney

ULC-S629 / UL-103HT listed stainless or lined masonry chimney, 6" flue, 15 feet (4.6 m.) minimum system height, exit 3 feet above the roof and two feet above anything within 10 feet. Dedicated flue; no air distribution duct; never in a fireplace.
Plumb and run the chimney

Plumb-bob from the exact centre of the flue to mark ceiling and roof; check joists and rafters and reconfirm clearances, then install the listed chimney from the ceiling to the rain cap per its instructions.
Connect the flue pipe

Slip the crimped end inside the stove collar and fix with three screws through the collar holes; stack the remaining lengths up to the chimney with the approved adapter, crimped ends down, 3 sheet metal screws per joint.
Combustion air

Room air through the ash box enclosure, or outside air from the floor (4" OAIR adapter) or the rear wall (4" Wall Air Intake) with 4"(100mm) i.d. flexible metal duct; secure the stove to the structure when using outside air.
Through-wall pass-through
Where the connector passes through a combustible wall, build one of the NFPA 211 systems A–D (12, 9, 6 or 2 in. to combustibles) and keep the vapour barrier intact.

NFPA 211 systems for passing the chimney connector through a combustible wall:

System A · 12 in. (305mm)Min. 3.5 in. (90 mm) brick wall; 12 in. (305 mm) of brick from the fireclay liner (min. 5/8 in. (16 mm) wall) to combustibles
System B · 9 in. (229mm)Solid-insulated listed factory-built chimney length, same inside diameter as the connector, 1 in. (25.4 mm) or more insulation, 9 in. (229 mm) air space
System C · 6 in. (152mm)24 gauge connector through a 24 gauge ventilated thimble with two 1 in. (25.4 mm) air channels, 6 in. (152 mm) glass fiber insulation
System D · 2 in. (51mm)Solid-insulated listed chimney section 2 in. (51 mm) larger than the connector, min. 12 in. (305 mm) long, connector spaced 1 in. (25.4 mm) on sheet steel plates, 2 in. (51 mm) air space

Fasteners must not penetrate the chimney liner; supports are fastened to wall surfaces on all sides. Maintain the vapour barrier wherever components penetrate to the exterior.
Mobile home requirements
Listed double-wall connector and ULC-S629 / UL-103HT chimney; outside air mandatory; legs anchored to the floor with 1/4 -20 x 2" lag screws; not in a sleeping room; keep the structure's integrity.

• Listed double-wall connector with a compatible ULC-S629 or UL-103HT listed chimney; horizontal connector not permitted.
  • Outside air supply must be used: 4" (102 mm) diameter metal air inlet ducting with rodent screen.
  • Anchor permanently: hook the supplied leg anchors around the bolts in the bottom of the legs and secure them to the floor with 1/4 -20 x 2" lag screws.
  • Do not install in a sleeping room; maintain the structural integrity of the floor, walls and ceiling/roof.
  • Do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance.

These are in addition to the residential requirements. Mobile home clearances (double-wall connector only) are shown as a diagram in Figure 11 on p. 20; see the double-wall clearance card.
Install the firebricks
Floor first (A and B at the ends of the ash dump, C against the rear post, D elsewhere), then the side walls, then the rear wall.

A1 1/2" x 4 1/2" x 1 1/4"
B4" x 4 1/2" x 1 1/4"
C7 1/4" x 4 1/2" x 1 1/4"
D9" x 4 1/2" x 1 1/4"
  1. Floor: the two small bricks (A and B) go at either end of the ash dump, regular D bricks elsewhere; the shorter C brick fits against the vertical post on the rear wall.
  2. Side walls: D bricks stand on end on top of the floor bricks. Set each between the tabs and slide it to the back.
  3. Rear wall last: stand each brick on end on the floor bricks, angle it under the tab, then push the bottom in until it rests against the back wall.

Firebrick set: 80000088. Brick rail set: 80002169.

Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted: inspect and clean

Not enough wood → unsplit wood preferred

Room air cover left on → check that it is removed
Chimney plugged or restricted → inspect and clean

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Start every fire with small, dry fuel and plenty of air.

  1. Move the air control to High (all the way to the left) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the stove. Crisscross several pieces of dry kindling on top, then add a few small pieces of dry wood.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully in flames. Don't leave the stove while the door is open.
  4. Add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. Once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, carry on with normal burning.
Never use gasoline, kerosene, lighter fluid or any other volatile liquid to start or "freshen up" a fire.

Your first two or three fires

The paint bakes on during the first 2-3 fires, and the smoke and fumes can bother some people. Open all the windows and doors. Bring the stove up slowly to a medium burn for about 45 minutes, then a high burn for another 45-60 minutes. Follow the Stove Bright paint sheet that came with the stove.

Smoke detectors may go off more often while the paint cures. Don't disconnect them.

air.title: Air control & reloading
air.html:
The air control sets how hard the fire burns. It runs from L (low) to H (high); high is all the way to the left.

Finding your setting

Every home is different, so finding the right setting takes some trial and error. Note what works for next time. If smoke pours down across the glass (a "waterfall"), you turned the air down too soon or too low.

For a clean burn, add two or three logs at a time and leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after loading. After about 30 minutes you can turn it down a lot.

Adding wood

  1. Turn the air control to high and let the fire brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff back into the room.
  3. Load dry logs endwise, up to 18" long, with space for air between them. Don't load wood so high, or in such a way, that opening the door would be hazardous.
Don't over-fire. A top or vent pipe glowing red means the stove is over-firing. That can permanently damage the stove and chimney, can be hazardous if it isn't corrected, and may void the warranty.

Optional blower

With the air on L, run the blower on Low. Between L and H, choose any speed. On Auto, the blower starts as the stove heats up and stops once it cools.

overnight.title: Overnight burns & restarting
overnight.html:
Setting up a long burn

  • Use unsplit logs. They're best for extended or overnight burns.
  • Char the new load completely with the air control on maximum before you turn it down for the night.
  • Don't try to burn overnight with green or wet wood.

Restarting in the morning

  1. Open the door and rake the hot embers toward the front of the stove.
  2. Add a couple of dry, split logs on top of the embers and close the door.
  3. Turn the air control to high. In a few minutes the logs should start burning.
  4. Once the wood has charred, set the air control back where you like it.
High (H) gives the maximum firing rate. Use it only to start a fire or get a fresh load going, not for everyday burning.

Won't last the night?

The air may be set too high (set it lower), there may not be enough wood (use unsplit logs), or the chimney may draw too hard because it's too tall or too wide.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood burns cleaner and more efficiently than softwood or freshly cut wood.

  • Season wood for six months or more and store it under cover, away from flames and heat.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.
  • The ideal length is 17 inches. The maximum is 18 inches.

Test a piece

Put a large piece on a good bed of coals. It's dry if it's burning on more than one side within one minute. It's damp if it turns black and lights within three minutes. If it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes, it's soaked. Don't burn it.

Never burn

Salt-water or treated wood, railroad ties, garbage, yard waste, cardboard or paper products, plywood or particleboard, coal or charcoal, plastic, rubber, paints or solvents, or building debris. Salt-water wood and garbage contain chlorides that quickly destroy metal and void the warranty. Never barbecue in the stove. Paper, sawdust or wax fire starters are fine for lighting.

ash.title: Removing the ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the stove is cold: once they're 3" to 4" deep and the fire has burned down and cooled. Always leave about 1" of ash on the firebox floor to help keep a hot bed of coals.

Using the ash dump

  1. The handle is under the ash lip, on the left. Pull it out 1/2" and turn it clockwise to unlock the dump.
  2. Hold the handle open and pull ashes into the opening. Leave large embers; they still hold heat.
  3. Release the handle and push it in to lock. Check the dump door is fully engaged, then fill the cavity with the remaining ash, level with the firebox floor.
  4. Lift and pull out the ash pan, empty it into a metal container, and seat the pan properly again.

Ash chute: to clear the ash lip, pull the ash pan out about 2", sweep the ash into the chute on the right side of the lip, and close the pan.

Never burn with the ash dump open. It creates a hazardous condition.

Keep ashes in a metal container with a tight lid, set on a non-combustible floor or the ground, well away from anything that burns, until every cinder is cold. Don't put other waste in it.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when the stove is cold, using fireplace glass cleaner. Never scrape it with anything that could scratch it, and don't use abrasive cleaners.

What the deposit tells you

  • Light brown and dusty, wipes off easily: good combustion and dry wood, so your pipes and chimney are likely fairly clean.
  • Black and greasy, hard to remove: wet or green wood and too slow a burn. The same deposit is building up in the chimney at least as fast.

A leaking door gasket can also dirty the glass. Check the gasket and the door latch.

Protect the glass

  • Don't slam the door, and make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass when you close it.
  • If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before you use the stove again. Use only 17-1/4" x 11-3/8" x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer.
Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires leave tar and moisture in the chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot: temperatures inside the chimney can exceed 2000°F (1100°C).

  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months during the heating season. Remove creosote once it's 3 mm or more.
  • Check daily until you learn how often you need to clean. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • Dry wood and plenty of air keep creosote down.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get ready to evacuate. Everyone should know the plan and the meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the stove (the air control).
  3. Call the fire department. Keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks, and check the combustibles around the chimney and the roof.
Pacific Energy strongly recommends having the chimney inspected by a certified professional (NFI, CSIA, WETT or APC).

care.title: Gaskets, bricks & regular checks
care.html:
Check these parts for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and bad warping:

WeeklyFirebricks for cracks · door gasket for sagging, placement or damage
MonthlyBrick rails and tabs · air riser tube at the back of the firebox · back of the airwash chamber · baffle locking pin · boost tube cover
At chimney cleaningTop baffle board/blanket · baffle · baffle gasket · top heat shield and bolt · brick rails · manifold
Every six monthsVacuum the grill openings of the optional blower
  • Door gasket: a 5/16" fiberglass rope that needs only light pressure to seal. Replace it when worn, using the kit from your dealer.
  • Baffle (at the top of the firebox): some warping, up to 1/4", is normal. More than that, or any crack or break, means it needs replacing.
  • Firebricks: replace broken or missing bricks.
  • Keep ash from piling up at the front of the firebox, where boost air comes in.
  • Clean a plated door with mild soap and water only; abrasive cleaners void the warranty.
Call your dealer about any damage. Running the stove with broken parts can damage other parts and may void the warranty.

safety.title: Safe use
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's running. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; touching it can burn skin.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning, and open it only to add wood. This stove isn't designed to burn with the door open.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep them well away from the stove.
  • Burn wood only. Other fuels, such as charcoal, can produce large amounts of carbon monoxide, a gas you can't smell or taste that can kill.
  • Burn directly on the firebricks. Don't raise the fire on a grate or andirons.
  • Don't alter the air control. Tampering is dangerous and voids the warranty, and the factory-set minimum burn rate must not be changed.
  • Don't store wood within the stove's clearances or in the space you need for loading and ash removal.
Detectors: Pacific Energy strongly recommends smoke and carbon monoxide detectors where the stove is installed.

Make sure everyone in the house knows how to run the stove safely and what to do in a chimney fire.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's warranty is for the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years)Parts only: porcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage, not impact), plating, firebox and baffle
3 year comprehensiveParts and labor on any defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets. Firebox rails and heat shields are left out of the lifetime coverage.
  • Labor under the lifetime coverage.
  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.

Early deterioration is a strong sign of improper use, such as excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel, and may void the warranty.

Need service? Contact your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, the model name and the serial number. The serial number is on the certification label and the cover of the manual. You can register the stove at pacificenergy.net/register.

specOutput.title: EPA rating & efficiency
specOutput.html:
EPA BTU output12,518 to 38,177 btu/hr
HHV tested efficiency71.3%
LHV tested efficiency77.1%
EPA certified emissions1.8 grams per hour
FuelSeasoned cord wood

Meets the U.S. EPA 2020 crib wood emission limits for wood heaters sold after May 15, 2020 (Method 28R); emissions testing by PFS-TECO Inc. Efficiencies are weighted averages tested to CSA B415. The output range uses CSA B415 efficiency and the low and high EPA test burn rates with Douglas Fir dimensional lumber.

Listed room heater, solid fuel type, also for use in mobile homes; certified to CAN/ULC S627 / UL 1482 (ETL#4001507). The minimum low burn rate is factory-set and must not be altered.

One rating set covers both the T5 LE and the T5 LE Classic; the manual gives no model-specific figures.

specWood.title: Wood length & loading
specWood.html:
Ideal wood length17 inches
Maximum wood length18 inches
FuelSeasoned cord wood

Load endwise, mixed shapes and diameters up to 18"(457mm), spaced for air flow; unsplit logs for extended or overnight burns. Burn directly on the firebricks, no grates or andirons. Wood should be air-dried six months or more.

specFlue.title: Chimney & connector
specFlue.html:
Flue outlet6 inches
ChimneyULC-S629 or UL-103HT listed stainless, or lined masonry suitable for solid fuel
Min. system height15 feet (4.6 m.) from base of appliance
Flue exit3 feet (1 m.) above roof; two feet (0.6 m) above highest projection within 10 feet (3 m)
Single-wall connectorSix inch, 24 gauge black pipe, clean and new; crimped ends down; 3 sheet metal screws at every joint and collar
Listed systemsCanada: ULC S-641 double wall connector + ULC-S629 chimney · USA: UL-103 HT connector and chimney

Keep the flue the same size as the 6" outlet; reducing or increasing it may hurt performance. Don't connect to a flue serving another appliance or to any air distribution duct, and don't install in a fireplace. The connector may not pass through an attic, roof space, closet or similar concealed space, floor or ceiling; wall pass-throughs per CAN/CSA-B365 (NFPA 211 systems on pp. 18-19). Figure 6 shows a 6" S.S. liner in a masonry chimney.

Up-and-out installs: 12" [300mm] minimum first section of pipe. The unit may be harder to start, so give the first section as much vertical length as possible.

Draft

Too much: excessive appliance temperatures, an uncontrollable burn, a glowing red stove part or chimney. Too little: back puffing into the room, chimney plugging, smoke leaking at appliance and connector joints.

specClearSW.html:

B. Backwall to unit8 in. / 203 mm

Confirm the single-wall connector clearance: the rating label (p. 3) lists E. backwall to connector as 15 in. / 380 mm, but the same label states a minimum clearance of 18 inches / 455 mm between a single-wall connector and combustible materials (reducible with listed pipe shields, wall protectors or other approved means). specFloor.title: Floor protector
specFloor.html:
On a combustible floor, use continuous non-combustible ember protection extending:

USA · front16" (406 mm) from the fuel loading door opening
USA · sides8" (203 mm) to the sides of the door opening
USA · minimum size33 3/8"(822mm) wide · 40 1/2"(1.03m) overall depth
Canada · firing side18" (457 mm)
Canada · other sides8" (203 mm)

Confirm the US side extension: p. 12 gives 8" (203 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening; the rating label (p. 3) lists G. 16 inches / 405 mm, H. 5 inches / 127 mm and I. 0 inches / 0 mm for the USA, with the letters marked on its drawing at the front, side and back.

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
ResidentialRoom air, or outside air (optional)
Mobile home · alcoveOutside air kit required
Through the floorHole for 4" metal venting behind the ash box enclosure; 4" OAIR adapter; 4"(100mm) i.d. flexible metal ducting
Through the wall4"(100mm) Wall Air Intake kit; 4" Intake Adapter over the hole in the rear of the ash box enclosure
Air inlet4" (102 mm) diameter, hooded or 90° elbow turned down, rodent screen

A floor intake must draw from a ventilated crawl space or be ducted outdoors; if the crawl space is well ventilated, the inlet need not be extended outside. With outside air in a residential install, secure the stove to the structure so the duct can't dislodge. Room air enters through the opening in the ash box enclosure; the troubleshooting chart lists a room air cover left in place as a cause of a stove that won't burn. Consult local code or CAN/CSA-B365 first.

Anything that creates negative pressure can pull fumes into the living space. In extreme cold, at very slow burn rates, the top of an exposed chimney can ice up and partly block the flue.

specBlower.title: Optional blower
specBlower.html:
KitWODC.BLOWB
Electrical rating (p. 20)115 volts A.C.-1.1 amps
Electrical rating (label)115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP
Fan output140 CFM

Three-prong power cord; can be installed at any time per the kit's instructions. Route the cord away from the heater, never under it. Rocker switch on the fan housing: Auto (fan starts as the stove reaches operating temperature and stops after it cools) or Man (bypasses the sensor). Speed: Low with the air control at L; any speed between L and H. Vacuum the grill openings at least every six months.

Confirm the blower current: the manual gives 115 volts A.C.-1.1 amps on p. 20 and 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP on the rating label (p. 3).

conflicts.issue: Blower electrical rating: '115 volts A.C.-1.1 amps' on p. 20 vs 'FAN ELECTRICAL RATING: 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP' on the rating label (p. 3).

US floor protector: p. 12 gives 16" (406 mm) to the front and 8" (203 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening (min. width 33 3/8", depth 40 1/2"); the rating label gives G. 16 INCHES / 405 MM, H. 5 INCHES / 127 MM, I. 0 INCHES / 0 MM for the USA (letters marked at front, side and back on the label drawing). Canada values agree (18/8/8).

The rating label lists the Alderlea T5 single-wall E. backwall to connector as 15 in. / 380 mm, but the same label states 'MINIMUM CLEARANCE BETWEEN SINGLE WALL CHIMNEY CONNECTOR AND COMBUSTIBLE MATERIALS-18INCHES/455MM' (reducible with listed shields) and adds 'AS TESTED - PIPE SHIELD MAY BE REQUIRED BY LOCAL AUTHORITIES'.

Clearance drawings show dimensions that are not among the label's lettered Alderlea T5 values. Figure 4 single-wall (p. 13): 8", 7", 18", 21", 14", 26", 7" vs label A 14 / B 8 / C 7 / D 23.5 / E 15 / F 21 in. Figure 4 double-wall (p. 13) and Figure 11 mobile home (p. 20) include 15" and 26" vs label E 12 / D 23.5 in. The drawings may measure to the flue centre; the text doesn't say. Flagged in both clearance drawers (specClearSW and specClearDW); values from the drawings not transcribed.

review.notes: Models: one manual covers both ('ALDERLEA T5 LE and ALDERLEA T5 LE Classic', p. 3). The cover and the rating label name only ALDERLEA T5 LE (the label is shared with SUPER LE and SUPER CLASSIC LE). No figure in the manual differs between the two models (dimensions, clearances, floor protector and parts are all captioned 'T5'/'T5 LE'), so the specs have no per-model rows. The catalog's 'Alderlea T5 Classic LE' is written 'ALDERLEA T5 LE Classic' in the manual. The parts list (p. 26) gives finishes Metalic Black paint, Sunset Red, Majolica Brown and Antique White enamel without saying which are the Classic; the catalog's 'Ivory' is not in the manual. Rating label p. 3: the layout text is scrambled; label/value pairs (LHV 77.1%, HHV 71.3%, EPA output 12,518 to 38,177 btu/hr, ideal 17 / max 18 inches, and the SUPER vs ALDERLEA T5 clearance columns) were matched using the reading-order extraction of the same page. Only the ALDERLEA T5 column was used. Not in the manual (left out): weight, firebox volume, heating area, maximum burn time, cordwood maximum BTU (catalog 72,000), non-catalytic design, cooktop/warming shelves, viewing/glass area. Catalog btu_output_epa 38,200 is the manual's 38,177 rounded, so not listed as a mismatch. Overall dimensions (Figure 1, p. 11) are a drawing with unlabeled values (25", 10 1/8", 28 3/4", 28 1/2", 29 3/4"), so no dimensions card. The '55" [1.4m] Minimum' on the venting drawings (pp. 16, 17, 21) is unlabeled and omitted. Canada floor protector minimum width is printed "41'(1.04m)" with a foot mark; shown as 1.04m with the printed form noted. The troubleshooting chart (p. 22) says 'see page 11' for excessive chimney height; p. 11 is Assembly/Dimensions (stale cross-reference). French-only: the label's French alcove note adds a width (LARGEUR 4 PIEDS/1.2M) not present in the English text; not included. The label limits 'do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance' to the USA; pp. 14 and 21 state it without that limit; the guide states it generally. p. 14 says 'both chimney system and connector must be listed' next to the single-wall black-pipe rules (on the label that line sits with the mobile home/alcove items); shown as printed. No code table; no gas-smell block (wood stove).
